requirements.requirement: Treat node1's /etc/inventory/app.conf as authoritative and mirror its content and deletion state to node2.
requirements.summary: A node1 test configuration appeared byte-for-byte on node2, and later removal on node1 removed the node2 copy. A second content-and-deletion cycle succeeded after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Automatically pick up changes from node1 on node2 within 15 minutes.
requirements.summary: The enabled persistent timer runs every minute. Direct automatic tests observed content propagation in about 54 seconds from source creation and deletion propagation in about 64 seconds from source deletion, comfortably within 15 minutes.

overall_summary: The task contract is satisfied. Direct transition tests demonstrate automatic, directional synchronization of both content and deletion well inside 15 minutes, including successful operation after restarts. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered services/configuration, and a successful post-restart end-to-end synchronization test.
limitations: The propagation tests used one representative content update and deletion rather than exhaustively testing every possible file change; the persistent one-minute timer and successful pre- and post-restart transitions provide strong supporting coverage.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene was strong: both test files were removed, no failed services or package damage were observed, and the task-required synchronization artifacts remained. One unnecessary transient mutation was identified: cmd-88c697e2862740a1 created or truncated known_hosts during a failed setup attempt; it was subsequently overwritten with valid content by cmd-611cfa2513094604 and did not remain as harmful residue. No other unnecessary mutations were identified.
